📰 General

Pakistan Conducts Border Strikes, Claims Death of 70 Militants in Afghanistan •

Pakistani forces launched a series of border strikes within Afghanistan targeting suspected militant hideouts. The operation, conducted early Sunday, resulted in the reported deaths of at least 70 individuals identified as Pakistani militants. Islamabad’s military attributed the attacks to these militants’ involvement in recent cross-border attacks originating within Afghanistan. The strikes occurred near the Durand Line, the contested border between the two countries.

🌍 World

Pope and Cardinals Participate in Annual Lenten Spiritual Exercises in Vatican •

The Spiritual Exercises for Lent commenced on February 22nd at 5 p.m. in the Pauline Chapel within Vatican City. The exercises, a longstanding tradition, were attended by Pope Leo XIV, Cardinals residing in Rome, and heads of various Vatican Dicasteries. The program, led by a designated preacher, is a core component of the Catholic Church’s Lenten observance. Participants engage in a structured reflection process designed to deepen their faith and prepare for Easter.

🦅 US

Gaudreau Celebrated by Team USA Following Historic Olympic Gold Medal Victory •

Following Team USA’s 2-1 overtime victory at the Olympic Winter Games Milano Cortina 2026, forward Johnny Gaudreau was honored by his teammates. Matthew Tkachuk and Zach Werenski wore a Gaudreau USA jersey after the game’s conclusion. The team expressed their appreciation for Gaudreau’s contributions during the tournament. This recognition occurred as Gaudreau competed with Team USA in the men’s hockey competition.

💰 Business

Bond Market Reversal: Rising Rates and Uncertainty Drive Bearish Sentiment •

The Treasury market is experiencing a shift in momentum, with investors increasingly favoring a bearish outlook. This change is driven by several factors, including the Supreme Court’s ruling against Trump’s tariffs and concerns about potential future interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve. Furthermore, persistent strength in the U.S. labor market is contributing to the downward pressure on bond prices. Analysts are observing heightened sell signals across the $31 trillion market as a result of these converging pressures.

💻 Technology

Google Earth Mishap Hilariously Ruined “Pluribus” Episode Reveal •

The seventh episode of the sci-fi series “Pluribus” was prematurely revealed due to a user’s accidental screenshot using Google Earth. A viewer unknowingly captured a significant scene from the episode while exploring a location in the show’s setting. Google’s historical imagery tool inadvertently exposed a key plot point to the public before the episode’s official release. This incident highlights the potential for unexpected leaks through readily available online resources.

🎭 Entertainment

Dennis Quaid Voices Conservative Views, Praises Reagan in New Interview •

Actor Dennis Quaid recently discussed his political views on Pastor Greg Laurie’s “The Greg Laurie Show,” expressing the belief that American politics have shifted too far to the left. Quaid’s comments stemmed from his role portraying President Ronald Reagan in the 2024 film “Reagan.” He emphasized a desire for a more balanced approach to political discourse. The interview generated discussion regarding Quaid’s perspective on contemporary American politics.

🏅 Sports

Crosby Ruled Out for Canada’s Gold Medal Game Due to Injury •

Sidney Crosby was unable to play for Team Canada in the gold medal game against the United States. The Canadian captain sustained a lower-body injury during the second period of their semi-final victory. This absence contributed to Canada’s 2-1 loss at Santagiulia Arena. The injury occurred earlier in the tournament, marking his second missed game for the team.

🔬 Science

Scientists Detect Unprecedented Gamma Ray Source, Challenging Cosmic Understanding •

Astronomers have identified a previously unknown source of extremely high-energy gamma rays, designated LHAASO J2108+5157. The object, located approximately 730 million light-years away, emits gamma rays with energies exceeding 100 TeV – significantly higher than typical astrophysical sources. Observations made by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) suggest the source’s origin remains unclear, prompting further investigation into its nature and potential mechanisms. Researchers are currently analyzing the data to determine the source’s composition and the processes generating these intense bursts of radiation.

🩺 Health

Lifelong Lead Exposure Linked to Increased Risk of Alzheimer’s and Dementia •

A new study has found a significant correlation between long-term lead exposure and an elevated risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias. Researchers discovered that individuals with the highest levels of lead stored in their bones exhibited a nearly three-fold increase in the likelihood of experiencing cognitive decline. The study reinforces previous research highlighting the detrimental effects of lead on neurological health over a lifetime. Further investigation is needed to fully understand the mechanisms behind this association and to determine optimal strategies for mitigation.
